phrases.japanese: こんにちは
phrases.notes: Safe all-purpose greeting during the day. Morning: おはようございます (Ohayou gozaimasu). Evening: こんばんは (Konbanwa).

responses.japanese: こんにちは！いらっしゃいませ！
responses.listen_for: いらっしゃいませ (Irasshaimase) is the standard shop/restaurant welcome chant. No response needed — just nod and smile.

responses.japanese: こんにちは、なにかおさがしですか？
responses.english: Hello, are you looking for something?
responses.listen_for: おさがし (お探し, osagashi) = looking for. Follow up with みているだけです (見ているだけです) if you're browsing.
responses.kanji: こんにちは、何かお探しですか？

phrases.japanese: ありがとうございます
phrases.notes: Use this constantly. Casual: ありがとう (Arigatou). You'll hear どういたしまして (Dou itashimashite) = you're welcome.

responses.japanese: どういたしまして
responses.listen_for: The formal response. Less common than you'd expect — Japanese often just smile or nod.

responses.japanese: いえ、どうぞ
responses.listen_for: A softer 'you're welcome'. どうぞ on its own means 'please go ahead / here you go'.

phrases.japanese: すみません
phrases.notes: Most useful word in Japan. Gets attention, apologizes lightly, lets you squeeze past someone.

responses.japanese: はい、どうぞ
responses.english: Yes, go ahead / Yes, what is it?
responses.listen_for: Staff responding to your attention-grab. They're ready to help — go ahead with your question.

responses.japanese: はい、なんでしょうか？
responses.english: Yes, what can I do for you?
responses.listen_for: Polite 'what do you need?' — follow with your question.
responses.kanji: はい、何でしょうか？

phrases.japanese: はい
phrases.notes: Also used to acknowledge listening. Very frequent.

responses.japanese: はい、はい
responses.listen_for: Repeated はい means 'I'm listening / I got it'. Very common in conversation.

phrases.japanese: いえ
phrases.notes: だいじょうぶです (大丈夫です, Daijoubu desu) is a softer way to decline.

responses.japanese: そうですか
responses.listen_for: Neutral acknowledgment. Not agreement or disagreement — just 'noted'.

phrases.japanese: わかりました
phrases.notes: Use after someone explains something. わかりません (わかりません (分かりません), Wakarimasen) = I don't understand.

responses.japanese: よかったです！
responses.listen_for: Relief expression — they're happy you understood.
responses.kanji: 良かったです！

phrases.japanese: わかりません
phrases.notes: Say this confidently rather than nodding along confused.

responses.japanese: えいごでいいましょうか？
responses.english: Shall I say it in English?
responses.listen_for: They're offering to switch to English. Say はい if you want that.
responses.kanji: 英語で言いましょうか？

responses.japanese: もういちどいいますね
responses.english: I'll say it one more time
responses.listen_for: They're going to repeat. Get ready to listen again.
responses.kanji: もう一度言いますね

phrases.japanese: もういちど、ゆっくりおねがいします
phrases.notes: Absolute lifesaver. Most people will happily comply.

responses.japanese: はい、ゆっくりいいますね
responses.listen_for: They'll slow right down. Focus on the key words — nouns and numbers.
responses.kanji: はい、ゆっくり言いますね

phrases.kanji: もう一度、ゆっくりお願いします

phrases.japanese: にほんごがあまりじょうずじゃないです
phrases.romaji: Nihongo ga amari jouzu ja nai desu
phrases.notes: Sets expectations well. People appreciate the honesty and effort.

responses.japanese: いえいえ、じょうずですよ！
responses.english: No no, you're good at it!
responses.listen_for: Japanese people will almost always say this even if your Japanese is minimal. It's encouragement, not assessment. Smile and say ありがとうございます.
responses.kanji: いえいえ、上手ですよ！

phrases.kanji: 日本語があまり上手じゃないです

phrases.japanese: えいごははなせますか？
phrases.notes: Ask before assuming. Common in tourist areas.

responses.japanese: すこしだけはなせます
responses.listen_for: すこし (少し, sukoshi) = a little. They'll try. Meet them halfway.
responses.kanji: 少しだけ話せます

responses.japanese: すみません、えいごはあまり…
responses.english: Sorry, my English is not great…
responses.listen_for: Trailing off with あまり means 'not much'. Switch to simple Japanese and gestures.
responses.kanji: すみません、英語はあまり…

responses.japanese: はい、すこしはなせます。どうぞ！
responses.english: Yes, I can speak a little. Go ahead!
responses.listen_for: Green light — they're willing to try English.
responses.kanji: はい、少し話せます。どうぞ！

phrases.japanese: よろしくおねがいします
phrases.english: Nice to meet you / Please take care of me
phrases.notes: Said when meeting someone, starting a transaction, or asking a favor.

responses.japanese: こちらこそ、よろしくおねがいします
responses.english: Likewise, pleased to meet you too
responses.listen_for: こちらこそ = 'the same to you / likewise'. The standard warm reply.
responses.kanji: こちらこそ、よろしくお願いします

phrases.kanji: よろしくお願いします

phrases.japanese: これはいくらですか？
phrases.notes: Point at the item. Listen for a number.

responses.japanese: 〜えんです
responses.listen_for: Just the number + えん (円, en). E.g., 1500えん = 1500 yen. If you don't catch it, ask: もういちどおねがいします (もう一度お願いします).
responses.kanji: 〜円です

responses.japanese: ぜいこみで〜えんになります
responses.listen_for: ぜいこみ (税込, zeikomi) = tax included. The final price.
responses.kanji: 税込で〜円になります

phrases.japanese: みているだけです
phrases.notes: Response to shop staff when browsing.

responses.japanese: ごゆっくりどうぞ
responses.listen_for: ゆっくり = slowly/at your pace. They're giving you space — no pressure.

responses.japanese: なにかありましたらおこえがけください
responses.english: Please let us know if you need anything
responses.listen_for: Long phrase, but just means 'call us if you need help'. Nod and browse.
responses.kanji: 何かありましたらお声がけください

phrases.japanese: これをください
phrases.notes: Point at item + say this. Works anywhere.

responses.japanese: ありがとうございます。〜えんになります
responses.english: Thank you. That will be [price] yen.
responses.listen_for: Listen for the number before えん (円). They'll often show you on a calculator or the register screen.
responses.kanji: ありがとうございます。〜円になります

responses.japanese: ふくろはごいりようですか？
responses.listen_for: ふくろ (袋, fukuro) = bag. Answer はい or いいえ.
responses.kanji: 袋はご入り用ですか？

phrases.japanese: ほかのいろはありますか？
phrases.romaji: Hoka no iro wa arimasu ka?
phrases.notes: Replace いろ (色, iro) / color with サイズ (saizu / size) if needed.

responses.japanese: はい、こちらにございます
responses.listen_for: こちら (kochira) = this way / over here. Follow them.

responses.japanese: もうしわけありませんが、このいろだけです
responses.romaji: Moushiwake arimasen ga, kono iro dake desu
responses.english: I'm sorry, we only have this color
responses.listen_for: もうしわけありません (申し訳ありません) = formal apology. だけ = only. They don't have other colors.
responses.kanji: 申し訳ありませんが、この色だけです

phrases.japanese: おおきいサイズはありますか？
phrases.english: Do you have a larger size?
phrases.notes: おおきい (大きい, ookii) = larger. ちいさい (小さい, chiisai) = smaller. Japanese sizing runs small.

responses.japanese: しょうしょうおまちください
responses.listen_for: しょうしょう (少々) = a brief moment. They're going to check the back. Stay put.
responses.kanji: 少々お待ちください

responses.japanese: ざいこをかくにんいたします
responses.listen_for: ざいこ (在庫, zaiko) = stock/inventory. They're checking for you.
responses.kanji: 在庫を確認いたします

phrases.kanji: 大きいサイズはありますか？

phrases.japanese: しちゃくできますか？
phrases.notes: For clothing stores.

responses.japanese: はい、こちらへどうぞ
responses.listen_for: They'll lead you to the fitting room. Follow them.

responses.japanese: フィッティングルームがあちらです
responses.english: The fitting room is over there
responses.listen_for: あちら (achira) = over there. They'll gesture the direction.

phrases.japanese: カードではらえますか？
phrases.notes: Japan is still cash-heavy. Always check.

responses.japanese: はい、クレジットカードはごりよういただけます
responses.romaji: Hai, kurejitto kaado wa go-riyou itadakemasu
responses.listen_for: クレジットカード = credit card. りよう (利用) = use/utilize. Green light.
responses.kanji: はい、クレジットカードはご利用いただけます

responses.japanese: もうしわけありませんが、げんきんのみです
responses.romaji: Moushiwake arimasen ga, genkin nomi desu
responses.listen_for: げんきん (現金, genkin) = cash. のみ = only. Find an ATM — 7-Eleven ATMs always work with foreign cards.
responses.kanji: 申し訳ありませんが、現金のみです

responses.japanese: Suicaはごりよういただけます
responses.listen_for: Many shops now accept IC cards like Suica as payment.
responses.kanji: Suicaはご利用いただけます

phrases.japanese: ふくろはいりません
phrases.notes: You'll be asked at konbini frequently.

responses.japanese: かしこまりました
responses.listen_for: Very formal acknowledgment. Common in service contexts. Same as わかりました (分かりました) but more polished.

phrases.japanese: めんぜいはできますか？
phrases.notes: Need passport. Purchase over ¥5,000.

responses.japanese: パスポートをおもちですか？
responses.listen_for: パスポート = passport. おもち (お持ち) = do you have. Always carry your passport in Japan.
responses.kanji: パスポートをお持ちですか？

responses.japanese: こちらのようしにごきにゅうください
responses.romaji: Kochira no youshi ni go-kinyuu kudasai
responses.listen_for: ようし (用紙, youshi) = form/paper. きにゅう (記入, kinyuu) = fill in. They'll hand you a tax exemption form.
responses.kanji: こちらの用紙にご記入ください

phrases.japanese: これはなんですか？
phrases.notes: Point at unfamiliar items.

responses.japanese: これは〜です
responses.listen_for: They'll name it. You might not know the word — that's fine. Smile and nod, or show interest with へえ！ (Hee! = Oh really!)

phrases.japanese: りょうしゅうしょをください
phrases.notes: For expense tracking or returns.

responses.japanese: はい、こちらがレシートです
responses.listen_for: レシート (reshiito) = receipt (casual). りょうしゅうしょ (領収書, ryoushuusho) = formal receipt. They may ask: あてなはどうしますか？ (宛名はどうしますか？, Atena wa dou shimasu ka?) = What name for the receipt?

phrases.japanese: ひとりです
phrases.notes: Hold up fingers too. They'll ask にんずうはおひとりさまですか？ (人数はお一人様ですか？, Ninzuu wa o-hitorisama desu ka?)

responses.japanese: しょうしょうおまちください
responses.listen_for: They're finding you a table. Wait by the entrance.
responses.kanji: 少々お待ちください

responses.japanese: こちらへどうぞ
responses.listen_for: Follow them — they're seating you now.

responses.japanese: ただいままんせきでございます
responses.listen_for: まんせき (満席, manseki) = full/no seats. You may need to wait or come back.
responses.kanji: ただいま満席でございます

phrases.japanese: なんめいさまですか？
phrases.english: How many people? (what staff will ask you)
phrases.notes: This is the question you'll hear at almost every restaurant entrance. Staff say なんめいさま (何名様, nanmei-sama) — the polite form. Your answers: 1ひとり (人, hitori), 2ふたり (人, futari), 3さんにん (人, san-nin). Always hold up fingers at the same time.

responses.japanese: おひとりさまですか？
responses.listen_for: Polite confirmation for solo diners. Answer はい to confirm.
responses.kanji: お一人様ですか？

responses.japanese: おふたりさまですね
responses.listen_for: Polite confirmation for two. はい to confirm.
responses.kanji: お二人様ですね

responses.japanese: おさんにんさまですね
responses.listen_for: Polite confirmation for three. はい to confirm.
responses.kanji: お三人様ですね

phrases.japanese: きんえんせきをおねがいします
phrases.notes: きねん (禁煙, kinen) = no smoking. きつえんせき (喫煙席, kitsuen-seki) = smoking section. Many restaurants in Japan still have both. Request this when being seated.

responses.japanese: きんえんせきにごあんないいたします
responses.english: I'll show you to a non-smoking seat
responses.listen_for: ごあんない (ご案内) = guide/lead. Follow them.
responses.kanji: 禁煙席にご案内いたします

responses.japanese: もうしわけありませんが、きんえんせきがまんせきです
responses.romaji: Moushiwake arimasen ga, kinen-seki ga manseki desu
responses.listen_for: まんせき (満席, manseki) = full. You may need to wait or accept a smoking seat.
responses.kanji: 申し訳ありませんが、禁煙席が満席です

phrases.kanji: 禁煙席をお願いします

phrases.japanese: カウンターせきでもいいですか？
phrases.notes: Staff may offer a counter seat (bar-style, solo or two people facing the kitchen) if tables are full. Solo diners are often seated here. You may hear this as a question — answer はい to accept or テーブルがいいです to request a table.

responses.japanese: カウンターせきでよろしければごあんないできます
responses.english: We can seat you at the counter if that's okay
responses.listen_for: よろしければ = if that's fine. Say はい、おねがいします (お願いします) to accept.
responses.kanji: カウンター席でよろしければご案内できます

phrases.kanji: カウンター席でもいいですか？

phrases.japanese: メニューをください
phrases.notes: Many places have picture menus.

responses.japanese: こちらがメニューになります
responses.listen_for: They'll hand it to you. English menus are common in tourist areas — you can ask: えいごのメニューはありますか？ (英語のメニューはありますか？, Eigo no menyuu wa arimasu ka?)

phrases.japanese: これをひとつください
phrases.notes: Point at menu item. ひとつ (一つ, hitotsu) = one. ふたつ (二つ, futatsu) = two.

responses.japanese: かしこまりました
responses.listen_for: Order received. They may follow with questions about spice, toppings, or cooking preference.

responses.japanese: からさはどうしますか？
responses.english: How spicy would you like it?
responses.listen_for: からさ (辛さ, karasa) = level of spice. Common at curry and ramen shops. Options usually: ふつう (普通, futsuu) / normal, からめ (辛め, karame) / spicier, からくなし (辛くなし, karaku nashi) / no spice.
responses.kanji: 辛さはどうしますか？

phrases.japanese: おすすめはなんですか？
phrases.notes: Staff love this question.

responses.japanese: 〜がとてもにんきです
responses.listen_for: にんき (人気, ninki) = popular. Remember the dish name they say and point at it on the menu.
responses.kanji: 〜がとても人気です

responses.japanese: きょうのおすすめは〜です
responses.listen_for: きょう (今日, kyou) = today. They're giving you their daily special.
responses.kanji: 今日のおすすめは〜です

phrases.japanese: おかいけいをおねがいします
phrases.notes: In Japan you usually pay at the register, not at the table.

responses.japanese: 〜えんでございます
responses.listen_for: Listen for the number. They'll often show the total on the register facing you.
responses.kanji: 〜円でございます

responses.japanese: レジでおしはらいください
responses.listen_for: レジ = register/cashier. Head to the front to pay.
responses.kanji: レジでお支払いください

phrases.kanji: お会計をお願いします

phrases.japanese: べつべつにはらえますか？
phrases.notes: べつべつ (別々, betsubetsu) = separately. Very useful for groups. Some restaurants may not support split bills — they may ask you to calculate and hand over separate cash instead.

responses.japanese: はい、しょうちしました
responses.listen_for: They'll split it at the register.
responses.kanji: はい、承知しました

responses.japanese: もうしわけありませんが、べつべつにはできません
responses.romaji: Moushiwake arimasen ga, betsubetsu ni wa dekimasen
responses.english: Sorry, we can't split the bill
responses.listen_for: できません = cannot. You'll need to settle among yourselves and pay together.
responses.kanji: 申し訳ありませんが、別々にはできません

phrases.japanese: おいしい！
phrases.notes: Say this to any chef or cook.

responses.japanese: ありがとうございます！
responses.listen_for: Pure joy. This is one of the best things you can say in Japan.

responses.japanese: よかったです！またきてください
responses.listen_for: またまたきて (来て, mata kite) = come again. High praise — they want you back.
responses.kanji: 良かったです！また来てください

phrases.japanese: たまごアレルギーがあります
phrases.notes: Swap allergen as needed.

responses.japanese: かくにんしてまいります
responses.listen_for: かくにん (確認, kakunin) = confirm/check. They're checking with the kitchen. Good sign.
responses.kanji: 確認してまいります

responses.japanese: もうしわけありませんが、〜がふくまれています
responses.romaji: Moushiwake arimasen ga, [allergen] ga fukumarete imasu
responses.listen_for: ふくまれています (含まれています, fukumarete imasu) = is contained/included. The dish has the allergen — avoid it.
responses.kanji: 申し訳ありませんが、〜が含まれています

phrases.kanji: 卵アレルギーがあります

phrases.japanese: からくしないでください
phrases.notes: Useful at ramen and curry shops.

responses.japanese: はい、かしこまりました
responses.listen_for: They got it. Your food will be mild.

phrases.kanji: 辛くしないでください

phrases.japanese: おみずをください
phrases.notes: Free in most restaurants.

responses.japanese: はい、すぐにおもちします
responses.english: Yes, I'll bring it right away
responses.listen_for: すぐ (sugu) = right away/immediately. Water is coming.
responses.kanji: はい、すぐにお持ちします

phrases.japanese: おみずを〇つおねがいします
phrases.notes: Ordering water for your group all at once. Hold up fingers to match the number.

responses.japanese: はい、すぐにおもちします
responses.english: Yes, I'll bring them right away
responses.listen_for: すぐ = right away. All glasses coming.
responses.kanji: はい、すぐにお持ちします

phrases.kanji: お水を〇つお願いします

phrases.japanese: もちかえりでおねがいします
phrases.notes: Konbini staff will ask: おあたためますか？ (温めますか？) (O-atatatemasu ka?)

responses.japanese: あたためますか？
responses.listen_for: Very common at konbini for hot food. はい、おねがいします (お願いします, hai, onegaishimasu) = yes please, だいじょうぶです (大丈夫です, daijoubu desu) = no thank you.
responses.kanji: 温めますか？

responses.japanese: おはしはおつけしますか？
responses.listen_for: おはし (お箸, ohashi) = chopsticks. They may also offer a fork (フォーク/fooku) or spoon (スプーン/supuun).
responses.kanji: お箸はお付けしますか？

phrases.kanji: 持ち帰りでお願いします

phrases.japanese: てんないでたべます
phrases.notes: Konbini staff will ask this.

responses.japanese: かしこまりました、イートインコーナーがあちらです
responses.romaji: Kashikomarimashita, iito in koonaa ga achira desu
responses.english: Understood, the eat-in corner is over there
responses.listen_for: イートイン (iito in) = eat-in area. あちら = over there. They'll gesture.

phrases.japanese: ラーメンはなんじかんまちますか？
phrases.romaji: Raamen wa nan jikan machimasu ka?
phrases.english: How long is the wait for ramen?
phrases.notes: Listen for みぬてs (分, minutes) or ほうrs (時間, hours).

responses.japanese: だいたい〜ふんほどおまちいただきます
responses.listen_for: だいたい (大体) = approximately. ふん (分) = minutes. They may hand you a ticket or buzzer.
responses.kanji: 大体〜分ほどお待ちいただきます

responses.japanese: せいりけんをどうぞ
responses.listen_for: せいりいけん (整理券, seiriiken) = numbered ticket. Hold on to it — your number will be called.
responses.kanji: 整理券をどうぞ

phrases.kanji: ラーメンは何時間待ちますか？

phrases.japanese: ふたりです
phrases.notes: ふたり (二人, futari) is irregular — not ni-nin. From three people onward the pattern becomes regular: さんにん (三人, san-nin), よにん (四人, yo-nin).

responses.japanese: こちらへどうぞ
responses.listen_for: Same seating phrase as for one person — follow them to your table.

responses.japanese: きんえんせきときつえんせきどちらがよろしいですか？
responses.romaji: Kin'en-seki to kitsuen-seki dochira ga yoroshii desu ka?
responses.listen_for: Rare now but some izakaya still ask. きねん (禁煙, kin'en) = non-smoking, きつえん (喫煙, kitsuen) = smoking.
responses.kanji: 禁煙席と喫煙席どちらがよろしいですか？

phrases.japanese: さんにんです
phrases.notes: さんにん (三人, san-nin) is the regular counter pattern used from 3 people onward (四人 yo-nin, 五人 go-nin, etc.).

responses.japanese: しょうしょうおまちください
responses.listen_for: Larger tables may take longer to free up.
responses.kanji: 少々お待ちください

responses.japanese: カウンターせきでもよろしいですか？
responses.listen_for: Some restaurants seat groups of 3 at the counter if tables are full.
responses.kanji: カウンター席でもよろしいですか？

phrases.japanese: ふたつください
phrases.notes: ふたつ (二つ, futatsu) = two, the generic item counter. Point at the menu.

responses.japanese: かしこまりました
responses.listen_for: Order received.

phrases.japanese: みっつください
phrases.notes: みっつ (三つ, mittsu) = three. The generic counter (一つ, 二つ, 三つ, 四つ, 五つ...) is irregular up through とお (十, too) = ten.

responses.japanese: かしこまりました
responses.listen_for: Order received.

phrases.japanese: べつべつにかいけいできますか？
phrases.notes: べつべつ (別々, betsubetsu) = separately. Some smaller shops in Japan don't allow split bills — ask before ordering if it matters.

responses.japanese: もうしわけございませんが、べつべつのおかいけいはできません
responses.romaji: Moushiwake gozaimasen ga, betsubetsu no okaikei wa dekimasen
responses.english: I'm sorry, we can't split the bill
responses.listen_for: べつべつ (別々, betsubetsu) = separate. You may need one person to pay and split later.
responses.kanji: 申し訳ございませんが、別々のお会計はできません

responses.japanese: かしこまりました、ではべつべつにごよういします
responses.romaji: Kashikomarimashita, dewa betsubetsu ni goyoui shimasu
responses.listen_for: Confirms they'll split the check for your group.
responses.kanji: かしこまりました、では別々にご用意します

phrases.japanese: いっしょにおねがいします
phrases.notes: Say this when asked べつべつですか、ごいっしょですか？ (別々ですか、ご一緒ですか？, Betsubetsu desu ka, go-issho desu ka?) — Separate or together?

responses.japanese: かしこまりました
responses.listen_for: One combined bill coming up.

phrases.japanese: 〜までいくらですか？
phrases.notes: Fill in the destination name.

responses.japanese: 〜えんです
responses.listen_for: Just the number + えん (円). Station machines also display fares on a map — use those to confirm.
responses.kanji: 〜円です

phrases.japanese: 〜はどこですか？
phrases.notes: Most useful navigation phrase.

responses.japanese: まっすぐいって、みぎにまがってください
responses.romaji: Massugu itte, migi ni magatte kudasai
responses.listen_for: まっすぐ = straight, みぎ (右, migi) = right, ひだり (左, hidari) = left, まがる (曲がる, magaru) = turn. These four words cover most direction answers.
responses.kanji: まっすぐ行って、右に曲がってください

responses.japanese: あそこです
responses.listen_for: あそこ = over there (far). They'll usually point. Look where they gesture.

responses.japanese: あるいて〜ふんぐらいです
responses.listen_for: あるいて (歩いて, aruite) = walking. ふん (分, fun) = minutes. ぐらい = approximately.
responses.kanji: 歩いて〜分ぐらいです

phrases.japanese: このバスは〜にいきますか？
phrases.romaji: Kono basu wa [destination] ni ikimasu ka?
phrases.notes: Replace バス (basu) with でんしゃ (電車, densha) / train if needed.

responses.japanese: はい、このバスでいけます
responses.english: Yes, you can get there on this bus
responses.listen_for: いけます (行けます, ikemasu) = can go. You're on the right bus.
responses.kanji: はい、このバスで行けます

responses.japanese: いいえ、〜ばんのバスにのってください
responses.romaji: Iie, [X] ban no basu ni notte kudasai
responses.listen_for: ばん (番, ban) = number [X]. のって (乗って, notte) = ride/take. Listen for the bus number.
responses.kanji: いいえ、〜番のバスに乗ってください

phrases.kanji: このバスは〜に行きますか？

phrases.japanese: つぎのえきはどこですか？
phrases.romaji: Tsugi no eki wa doko desu ka?
phrases.notes: Announcements on most lines are bilingual.

responses.japanese: つぎは〜えきです
responses.listen_for: つぎわ (次は, tsugi wa) = next is. えき (駅, eki) = [name] station.
responses.kanji: 次は〜駅です

phrases.japanese: 〜ばんせんはどこですか？
phrases.notes: Very useful in large stations like Shinjuku.

responses.japanese: 〜ばんせんにあちらです
responses.listen_for: あちら = over there. They'll point. Follow the signs — platform numbers are clearly posted.
responses.kanji: 〜番線にあちらです

phrases.japanese: タクシーをおねがいします
phrases.notes: Doors open automatically — don't touch them.

responses.japanese: どちらまでですか？
responses.listen_for: どちら = where (polite). Show your destination in Japanese text on your phone — drivers appreciate this.

phrases.kanji: タクシーをお願いします

phrases.japanese: ここでとめてください
phrases.notes: For taxis.

responses.japanese: 〜えんになります
responses.listen_for: The fare total. Taxis in Japan are metered and reliable. Always pay exact if possible.
responses.kanji: 〜円になります

phrases.kanji: ここで止めてください

phrases.japanese: のりかえはありますか？
phrases.notes: For complex train routes.

responses.japanese: 〜えきでのりかえてください
responses.listen_for: のりかえて (乗り換えて, norikaete) = transfer. えき (駅) = station name. Note the station name carefully.
responses.kanji: 〜駅で乗り換えてください

responses.japanese: のりかえなしでいけます
responses.listen_for: なし (nashi) = without. Direct route — stay on the train.
responses.kanji: 乗り換えなしで行けます

phrases.kanji: 乗り換えはありますか？

phrases.japanese: でぐちはどこですか？
phrases.notes: Big stations have numbered/lettered exits.

responses.japanese: 〜ばんでぐちがあちらです
responses.listen_for: ばん (番) = number. あちら = over there. All exits are signposted — follow the kanji for your number.
responses.kanji: 〜番出口があちらです

phrases.japanese: Suicaはどこでかえますか？
phrases.romaji: Suica wa doko de kaemasu ka?
phrases.english: Where can I buy a Suica card?
phrases.notes: Get one at the airport.

responses.japanese: けんばいきでおかいもとめいただけます
responses.english: You can purchase one at the ticket machine
responses.listen_for: けんばいき (券売機, kenbaiki) = ticket vending machine. They'll point you to it.
responses.kanji: 券売機でお買い求めいただけます

phrases.japanese: きっぷをにまいください
phrases.notes: まい (枚, mai) counts flat thin objects like tickets and paper: 1いちまい (枚, ichimai), 2にまい (枚, nimai), 3さんまい (枚, sanmai).

responses.japanese: かたみちですか、おうふくですか？
responses.romaji: Katamichi desu ka, oufuku desu ka?
responses.listen_for: かたみち (片道, katamichi) = one-way, おうふく (往復, oufuku) = round-trip.
responses.kanji: 片道ですか、往復ですか？

phrases.japanese: タクシーはさんにんのれますか？
phrases.english: Can three people fit in this taxi?
phrases.notes: Standard Japanese taxis seat up to 4 passengers; larger groups need a ジャンボタクシー (jumbo taxi).

responses.japanese: はい、だいじょうぶです
responses.listen_for: Confirms your group fits.
responses.kanji: はい、大丈夫です

responses.japanese: よにんまでです
responses.listen_for: 4よにんまで (人まで, yonin made) = up to 4 people — standard taxi capacity.
responses.kanji: 4人までです

phrases.kanji: タクシーは3人乗れますか？

phrases.japanese: チェックインをおねがいします
phrases.notes: They'll ask for your passport.

responses.japanese: パスポートをおねがいします
responses.listen_for: Standard for all foreign guests. Hand it over.
responses.kanji: パスポートをお願いします

responses.japanese: こちらにサインをおねがいします
responses.listen_for: サイン (sain) = signature. They'll show you where.
responses.kanji: こちらにサインをお願いします

responses.japanese: おへやは〜かいです
responses.listen_for: かい (階, kai) = floor number. 1いっかい (階, ikkai) = 1F. They'll hand you the key card too.
responses.kanji: お部屋は〜階です

phrases.kanji: チェックインをお願いします

phrases.japanese: 〇めいでよやくした〜です
phrases.english: I have a reservation for ___ people under [name]
phrases.notes: Combine the number of guests with your name when checking in as a group. めい (名, mei) is the formal counter for people used in hotels and restaurants.

responses.japanese: しょうしょうおまちください、かくにんいたします
responses.english: Please wait a moment, I'll confirm
responses.listen_for: They're pulling up your reservation.
responses.kanji: 少々お待ちください、確認いたします

responses.japanese: はい、ごよやくをかくにんいたしました
responses.listen_for: かくにん (確認) = confirmed. You're checked in.
responses.kanji: はい、ご予約を確認いたしました

phrases.japanese: よやくした〜です
phrases.notes: Fill in your name.

responses.japanese: しょうしょうおまちください、かくにんいたします
responses.english: Please wait a moment, I'll confirm
responses.listen_for: They're pulling up your reservation. Wait.
responses.kanji: 少々お待ちください、確認いたします

responses.japanese: はい、ごよやくをかくにんいたしました
responses.listen_for: かくにん (確認) = confirmed. You're checked in.
responses.kanji: はい、ご予約を確認いたしました

phrases.japanese: へやのかぎをなくしました
phrases.notes: Hopefully not needed.

responses.japanese: へやばんごうをおしえていただけますか？
responses.romaji: Heya bangou wo oshiete itadakemasu ka?
responses.english: Could you tell me your room number?
responses.listen_for: へやばんごう (部屋番号, heya bangou) = room number. Tell them your floor and room.
responses.kanji: 部屋番号を教えていただけますか？

phrases.kanji: 部屋の鍵をなくしました

phrases.japanese: タオルをもっとください
phrases.notes: Replace タオル (taoru) with pillow, blanket, etc.

responses.japanese: すぐにおもちいたします
responses.listen_for: すぐ = right away. They'll deliver to your room.
responses.kanji: すくにお持ちいたします

phrases.japanese: Wi-Fiのパスワードはなんですか？
phrases.romaji: Wi-Fi no pasuwaado wa nan desu ka?
phrases.notes: Often on a card in the room.

responses.japanese: こちらのカードをごらんください
responses.romaji: Kochira no kaado wo goran kudasai
responses.listen_for: They'll hand you a card or point to one in the room with the password printed on it.
responses.kanji: こちらのカードをご覧ください

phrases.kanji: Wi-Fiのパスワードは何ですか？

phrases.japanese: チェックアウトはなんじですか？
phrases.romaji: Chekku auto wa nanji desu ka?
phrases.notes: Usually 11:00 or 12:00.

responses.japanese: チェックアウトは〜じでございます
responses.romaji: Chekku auto wa [X] ji de gozaimasu
responses.listen_for: じ (時, ji) = o'clock. Listen for the number before じ (時).
responses.kanji: チェックアウトは〜時でございます

responses.japanese: レイトチェックアウトをごきぼうですか？
responses.romaji: Reito chekku auto wo go-kibou desu ka?
responses.english: Would you like a late checkout?
responses.listen_for: レイトチェックアウト = late checkout. きぼう (希望, kibou) = wish/desire. There's usually a fee.
responses.kanji: レイトチェックアウトをご希望ですか？

phrases.kanji: チェックアウトは何時ですか？

phrases.japanese: にもつをあずかってもらえますか？
phrases.notes: Japanese hotels excel at this.

responses.japanese: はい、なんじまでおあずかりしますか？
responses.romaji: Hai, nanji made oazukari shimasu ka?
responses.english: Yes, until what time shall we hold it?
responses.listen_for: なんじまで (何時まで, nanji made) = until what time. Tell them your pickup time.
responses.kanji: はい、何時までお預かりしますか？

phrases.kanji: 荷物を預かってもらえますか？

phrases.japanese: ちかくにおすすめのレストランはありますか？
phrases.romaji: Chikaku ni osusume no resutoran wa arimasu ka?
phrases.english: Are there any recommended restaurants nearby?
phrases.notes: Hotel staff recommendations are gold.

responses.japanese: 〜がとてもおいしいですよ
responses.listen_for: とても (totemo) = very. They'll name a place. Ask them to write it down: かいてもらえますか？ (書いてもらえますか？, Kaite moraemasu ka?)
responses.kanji: 〜がとても美味しいですよ

phrases.kanji: 近くにおすすめのレストランはありますか？

phrases.japanese: ふたりべやをおねがいします
phrases.notes: ふたりべや (二人部屋, futari-beya) = twin/double room. ひとりべや (一人部屋, hitori-beya) = single, さんにんべや (三人部屋, san-nin-beya) = triple.

responses.japanese: ツインとダブル、どちらがよろしいですか？
responses.romaji: Tsuin to daburu, dochira ga yoroshii desu ka?
responses.english: Twin or double, which would you prefer?
responses.listen_for: ツイン (tsuin) = two separate beds, ダブル (daburu) = one large shared bed.

phrases.kanji: 二人部屋をお願いします

phrases.japanese: さんにんべやはありますか？
phrases.english: Do you have a room for three?
phrases.notes: Triple rooms are less common in Japan — many hotels max out at 2 per room, so you may need an extra bed or a separate room.

responses.japanese: もうしわけございませんが、まんしつです
responses.listen_for: まんしつ (満室, manshitsu) = fully booked rooms — different from まんせき (満席, manseki) = full seats.
responses.kanji: 申し訳ございませんが、満室です

responses.japanese: エキストラベッドをごよういできます
responses.english: We can provide an extra bed
responses.listen_for: エキストラベッド (ekisutora beddo) = extra bed, often a solution for a third guest.
responses.kanji: エキストラベッドをご用意できます

phrases.kanji: 三人部屋はありますか？

phrases.japanese: カウンターにすわってもいいですか？
phrases.romaji: Kauntaa ni suwatte mo ii desu ka?
phrases.english: May I sit at the bar counter?
phrases.notes: Sitting at the counter is the move in Japan.

responses.japanese: はい、どうぞ、こちらへ
responses.listen_for: どうぞ = please go ahead. こちらへ = this way. You're in.

responses.japanese: もうしわけありませんが、カウンターはまんせきです
responses.romaji: Moushiwake arimasen ga, kauntaa wa manseki desu
responses.listen_for: まんせき (満席, manseki) = full. Ask: テーブルせきはありますか？ (テーブル席はありますか？) (Is there a table?)
responses.kanji: 申し訳ありませんが、カウンターは満席です

phrases.kanji: カウンターに座ってもいいですか？

phrases.japanese: 〇にんでテーブルにすわれますか？
phrases.english: Can ___ of us sit at a table?
phrases.notes: Use this when entering a bar as a group. Some standing bars (立ち飲み/tachinomi) may only have counter seating.

responses.japanese: はい、こちらへどうぞ
responses.listen_for: Follow them to the table or counter.

responses.japanese: テーブルはしょうしょうおまちいただけますか？
responses.romaji: Teeburu wa shoushou omachi itadakemasu ka?
responses.english: Could you wait a moment for a table?
responses.listen_for: They're clearing a table. Say はい to wait.
responses.kanji: テーブルは少々お待ちいただけますか？

phrases.kanji: 〇人でテーブルに座れますか？

phrases.japanese: おすすめのカクテルはありますか？
phrases.romaji: Osusume no kakuteru wa arimasu ka?
phrases.english: Do you have a recommended cocktail?
phrases.notes: This will get you the bartender's best work.

responses.japanese: こんやは〜がおすすめです
responses.listen_for: こんや (今夜, konya) = tonight. They'll name the drink. Nod and say それをおねがいします (お願いします).
responses.kanji: 今夜は〜がおすすめです

responses.japanese: どんなおさけがおすきですか？
responses.romaji: Donna osake ga osuki desu ka?
responses.english: What kind of drinks do you like?
responses.listen_for: Great sign — they want to personalize. Describe: のtすぇえt (甘くない, not sweet), フルーツィー (fruity), stろんg (強い, strong), ぃght (軽い, light).
responses.kanji: どんなお酒がお好きですか？

phrases.japanese: ウイスキーのリストをみせてください
phrases.romaji: Uisukii no risuto wo misete kudasai
phrases.english: Can I see the whisky list?
phrases.notes: Japan has incredible domestic whisky.

responses.japanese: こちらがウイスキーリストです
responses.listen_for: They'll hand you the list. Take your time — these lists can be extensive.

responses.japanese: こくさんとゆにゅう、どちらがよろしいですか？
responses.romaji: Kokusan to yunyuu, dochira ga yoroshii desu ka?
responses.english: Would you prefer domestic or imported?
responses.listen_for: こくさん (国産, kokusan) = domestic/Japanese. ゆにゅう (輸入, yunyuu) = imported. You're here for こくさん (国産).
responses.kanji: 国産と輸入、どちらがよろしいですか？

phrases.kanji: ウイスキーのリストを見せてください

phrases.japanese: これはどんなあじですか？
phrases.romaji: Kore wa donna aji desu ka?
phrases.notes: Key flavour words: すぇえt (甘い, sweet), dry (辛口, dry), びってr (苦い, bitter), そうr (酸っぱい, sour), フルーツィー (fruity).

responses.japanese: あまくて、すこしフルーツィーです
responses.english: It's sweet and a little fruity
responses.listen_for: あまい (甘い) = sweet, すこし (少し) = a little, フルーツィー = fruity. Combine these words to understand the profile.
responses.kanji: 甘くて、少しフルーツィーです

responses.japanese: からくちでスモーキーなあじわいです
responses.romaji: Karakuchi de sumoookii na ajiwai desu
responses.english: It has a dry, smoky flavor
responses.listen_for: からくち (辛口, karakuchi) = dry. スモーキー = smoky. あじわい (味わい, ajiwai) = flavor/taste profile.
responses.kanji: 辛口でスモーキーな味わいです

responses.japanese: かんきつけいのかおりとハーブのようなあとあじがあります
responses.romaji: Kankitsu-kei no kaori to haabu no you na ato-aji ga arimasu
responses.english: It has a citrus aroma with an herbal finish
responses.listen_for: かんきつ (柑橘, kankitsu) = citrus. かおり (香り, kaori) = aroma. あとあじ (後味, atoaji) = finish/aftertaste. You're getting a real cocktail description.
responses.kanji: 柑橘系の香りとハーブのような後味があります

phrases.kanji: これはどんな味ですか？

phrases.japanese: もういっぱいおねがいします
phrases.notes: いっぱい (一杯) = one glass/drink.

responses.japanese: かしこまりました
responses.listen_for: Order received. Same again is coming.

responses.japanese: おなじものでよろしいですか？
responses.romaji: Onaji mono de yoroshii desu ka?
responses.listen_for: おなじ (同じ, onaji) = same. They're confirming you want a repeat. Say はい or point to something new on the menu.
responses.kanji: 同じものでよろしいですか？

phrases.kanji: もう一杯お願いします

phrases.japanese: あまくないものがすきです
phrases.romaji: Amaku nai mono ga suki desu
phrases.notes: Great for directing the bartender.

responses.japanese: では、〜はいかがですか？
responses.listen_for: では (dewa) = then/in that case. いかが = how about? They're tailoring a recommendation. Say おねがいします (お願いします).

phrases.kanji: 甘くないものが好きです

phrases.japanese: これはなにのベーススピリッツですか？
phrases.romaji: Kore wa nani no beesu supirittsu desu ka?
phrases.english: What is the base spirit in this?
phrases.notes: Shows genuine cocktail knowledge.

responses.japanese: ベースは〜をつかっています
responses.listen_for: つかっています (使っています, tsukatte imasu) = is using. They'll name the spirit. You might also hear じかせい (自家製, jikasei) = house-made.
responses.kanji: ベースは〜を使っています

phrases.kanji: これは何のベーススピリッツですか？

phrases.japanese: にほんのウイスキーをためしてみたいです
phrases.romaji: Nihon no uisukii wo tameshite mitai desu
phrases.english: I'd like to try a Japanese whisky
phrases.notes: Opens the door to Nikka, Suntory, craft expressions.

responses.japanese: シングルモルトとブレンデッド、どちらがよろしいですか？
responses.romaji: Shinguru moruto to burendeddo, dochira ga yoroshii desu ka?
responses.english: Would you prefer single malt or blended?
responses.listen_for: シングルモルト = single malt. ブレンデッド = blended. A real whisky conversation just started.

responses.japanese: ニッカとサントリー、どちらのほうがすきですか？
responses.romaji: Nikka to Santori, dochira no hou ga suki desu ka?
responses.english: Do you prefer Nikka or Suntory?
responses.listen_for: The two big houses. If you don't know yet, say まだいどんtkのwいぇt (わかりません (分かりません), I don't know yet).
responses.kanji: ニッカとサントリー、どちらの方が好きですか？

phrases.kanji: 日本のウイスキーを試してみたいです

phrases.japanese: ハイボールをおねがいします
phrases.notes: Japan's most popular bar drink. Ridiculously well-made.

responses.japanese: ウイスキーはなにになさいますか？
responses.romaji: Uisukii wa nani ni nasaimasu ka?
responses.listen_for: なにになさいますか (何になさいますか) = what will you have? They're asking which whisky for your highball.
responses.kanji: ウイスキーは何になさいますか？

responses.japanese: こさはいかがしますか？
responses.english: How strong would you like it?
responses.listen_for: こさ (濃さ, kosa) = strength/concentration. こいめ (濃いめ, koime) = stronger, うすめ (薄め, usume) = weaker, ふつう (普通, futsuu) = standard.
responses.kanji: 濃さはいかがしますか？

phrases.kanji: ハイボールをお願いします

phrases.japanese: かんぱい！
phrases.notes: Make eye contact with each person as you clink.

responses.japanese: かんぱい！
responses.listen_for: They'll echo it back. Make eye contact — not doing so is considered rude.
responses.kanji: 乾杯！

phrases.japanese: ノンアルコールのカクテルはありますか？
phrases.romaji: Non-arukooru no kakuteru wa arimasu ka?
phrases.notes: Mocktail culture is growing in Japan.

responses.japanese: はい、モクテルをごよういしております
responses.romaji: Hai, mokuteru wo go-youi shite orimasu
responses.listen_for: モクテル = mocktail. ごようい (ご用意, go-youi) = prepared/available.
responses.kanji: はい、モクテルをご用意しております

responses.japanese: もうしわけありませんが、アルコールのみです
responses.romaji: Moushiwake arimasen ga, arukooru nomi desu
responses.listen_for: のみ = only. Not every bar does mocktails yet, especially traditional ones.
responses.kanji: 申し訳ありませんが、アルコールのみです

phrases.japanese: バーテンダーさんはどれくらいこのバーではたらいていますか？
phrases.romaji: Baatendaa-san wa dorekurai kono baa de hataraite imasu ka?
phrases.english: How long have you been working at this bar?
phrases.notes: Great conversation starter. Japanese bartenders train for years.

responses.japanese: 〜ねんになります
responses.listen_for: ねん (年, nen) = years. A bartender saying 10ねん (年, juunen) / 10 years or more is not unusual.
responses.kanji: 〜年になります

responses.japanese: しゅぎょうは〜ねんしました
responses.listen_for: しゅぎょう (修行, shugyou) = training/apprenticeship. This is the craft tradition — they apprenticed under a master.
responses.kanji: 修行は〜年しました

phrases.kanji: バーテンダーさんはどれくらいこのバーで働いていますか？

phrases.japanese: このカクテルのつくりかたをおしえてもらえますか？
phrases.romaji: Kono kakuteru no tsukurikata wo oshiete moraemasu ka?
phrases.english: Could you tell me how this cocktail is made?
phrases.notes: Japanese bartenders will give you a thorough, proud answer.

responses.japanese: まず〜をつかって、つぎに〜をくわえます
responses.romaji: Mazu [ingredient] wo tsukatte, tsugi ni [ingredient] wo kuwaemasu
responses.english: First I use [ingredient], then I add [ingredient]
responses.listen_for: まず (mazu) = first. つぎに (次に, tsugi ni) = next. くわえます (加えます, kuwaemasu) = add.
responses.kanji: まず〜を使って、次に〜を加えます

phrases.kanji: このカクテルの作り方を教えてもらえますか？

phrases.japanese: こんやのスペシャルはなんですか？
phrases.romaji: Konya no supesharu wa nan desu ka?
phrases.notes: Seasonal and nightly specials are common.

responses.japanese: こんやは〜をつかったきせつのカクテルです
responses.romaji: Konya wa [ingredient] wo tsukatta kisetsu no kakuteru desu
responses.english: Tonight it's a seasonal cocktail using [ingredient]
responses.listen_for: きせつ (季節, kisetsu) = seasonal. つかった (使った, tsukatta) = using. This is the bartender's creative pick.
responses.kanji: 今夜は〜を使った季節のカクテルです

phrases.kanji: 今夜のスペシャルは何ですか？

phrases.japanese: おみずもいっしょにいただけますか？
phrases.romaji: Omizu mo issho ni itadakemasu ka?
phrases.english: Could I also have some water?
phrases.notes: Stay hydrated — Japanese cocktails are deceptively smooth.

responses.japanese: はい、もちろんです
responses.listen_for: もちろんです = of course. Completely normal to ask.

phrases.kanji: お水も一緒にいただけますか？

phrases.japanese: ふたりぶんおねがいします
phrases.notes: 〜にんぶん (人分, -nin bun) = portions for X people. Useful for sharing plates: ふたりぶん (二人分, futari-bun), さんにんぶん (三人分, san-nin bun).

responses.japanese: かしこまりました
responses.listen_for: Order received for the group.

phrases.japanese: さんにんできました
phrases.notes: 〜にんできました (人で来ました, -nin de kimashita) = we came as a group of X. Useful when a host asks your party size.

responses.japanese: なんめいさまですか？
responses.listen_for: Polite way to ask party size — answer with ひとり/ふたり/さんにん (一人/二人/三人) etc.
responses.kanji: 何名様ですか？

responses.japanese: カウンターせきになりますがよろしいですか？
responses.romaji: Kauntaa-seki ni narimasu ga yoroshii desu ka?
responses.english: It will be counter seating, is that okay?
responses.listen_for: Common for small bars when tables don't fit your group size.
responses.kanji: カウンター席になりますがよろしいですか？

phrases.japanese: 〜にいきたいんですが
phrases.notes: The んですが softens it into a request.

responses.japanese: ここからあるいて〜ぶんぐらいです
responses.romaji: Koko kara aruite [X] fun gurai desu
responses.english: It's about [X] minutes walk from here
responses.listen_for: あるいて (歩いて, aruite) = walking. ふん (分) = minutes. ぐらい = about/approximately.
responses.kanji: ここから歩いて〜分ぐらいです

responses.japanese: でんしゃでいったほうがいいですよ
responses.romaji: Densha de itta hou ga ii desu yo
responses.english: It's better to go by train
responses.listen_for: でんしゃ (電車, densha) = train. ほうがいい (方がいい) = better to. They're steering you to public transport.
responses.kanji: 電車で行った方がいいですよ

phrases.japanese: まっすぐいってください
phrases.notes: Key direction words: まっすぐ/みぎ/ひだり (右/左).

responses.japanese: 〜メートルさきに〜があります
responses.listen_for: メートル = meters. さき (先, saki) = ahead. They're giving you a landmark to aim for.
responses.kanji: 〜メートル先に〜があります

phrases.kanji: まっすぐ行ってください

phrases.japanese: ここからとおいですか？
phrases.notes: ちかいです (近いです, chikai desu) = it is close.

responses.japanese: いいえ、ちかいですよ。あるいて〜ふんです
responses.romaji: Iie, chikai desu yo. Aruite [X] fun desu
responses.english: No, it's close. [X] minutes on foot
responses.listen_for: ちかい (近い, chikai) = close/nearby. あるいて (歩いて) = walking. The number before ふん (分) is your walk time.
responses.kanji: いいえ、近いですよ。歩いて〜分です

responses.japanese: すこしとおいです。バスかでんしゃがいいですよ
responses.romaji: Sukoshi tooi desu. Basu ka densha ga ii desu yo
responses.english: It's a bit far. Bus or train would be better
responses.listen_for: すこしとおい (少し遠い, sukoshi tooi) = a bit far. か = or. They're recommending transport.
responses.kanji: 少し遠いです。バスか電車がいいですよ

phrases.japanese: ちずをえがいてもらえますか？
phrases.english: Could you draw me a map?
phrases.notes: Japanese people are incredibly helpful — many will walk you there.

responses.japanese: はい、ちょっとまってください
responses.listen_for: ちょっとまってください (ちょっと待ってください) = wait a moment. They're grabbing a pen or phone.
responses.kanji: はい、ちょっと待ってください

responses.japanese: いっしょにいきましょうか？
responses.listen_for: いっしょに (一緒に, issho ni) = together. いきましょうか (行きましょうか) = shall we go? They're offering to escort you. Say ありがとうございます!
responses.kanji: 一緒に行きましょうか？

phrases.kanji: 地図を描いてもらえますか？

phrases.japanese: トイレはどこですか？
phrases.notes: Japanese public toilets are world-class.

responses.japanese: あちらです
responses.listen_for: あちら = over there. They'll point. Follow the direction.

responses.japanese: 〜かいにございます
responses.listen_for: かい (階, kai) = floor. In department stores toilets are often on a specific floor.
responses.kanji: 〜階にございます

phrases.japanese: たすけてください！
phrases.notes: Loud and clear. People will respond.

responses.japanese: どうしましたか？
responses.listen_for: どうしましたか = what's wrong / what happened? Be ready to point or show a translation.

phrases.japanese: きゅうきゅうしゃをよんでください
phrases.notes: Emergency numbers: 119 (ambulance/fire), 110 (police).

responses.japanese: すぐによびます
responses.listen_for: すぐ = immediately. Help is being called.
responses.kanji: すぐに呼びます

phrases.kanji: 救急車を呼んでください

phrases.japanese: パスポートをなくしました
phrases.notes: Go to the nearest こうばん (交番, koban) / police box first.

responses.japanese: こうばんにいってください
responses.english: Please go to the police box
responses.listen_for: こうばん (交番, kouban) = small police box/koban. These are everywhere in Japan and very helpful.
responses.kanji: 交番に行ってください

responses.japanese: いつ、どこでなくしましたか？
responses.english: When and where did you lose it?
responses.listen_for: いつ = when. どこ = where. Answer as best you can.

phrases.japanese: ぐあいがわるいです
phrases.notes: いたい (痛い, itai) = it hurts. Point at where.

responses.japanese: どこがいたいですか？
responses.listen_for: どこ = where. いたい (痛い) = hurt/pain. Point at the affected area.
responses.kanji: どこが痛いですか？

responses.japanese: びょういんにいったほうがいいです
responses.romaji: Byouin ni itta hou ga ii desu
responses.english: You should go to a hospital
responses.listen_for: びょういん (病院, byouin) = hospital. ほうがいい (方がいい) = should/better to.
responses.kanji: 病院に行った方がいいです

phrases.japanese: たいしかんにでんわしてください
phrases.notes: Know your country's embassy number before you go.

responses.japanese: わかりました。どこのくにですか？
responses.romaji: Wakarimashita. Doko no kuni desu ka?
responses.listen_for: どこのどこのくに (国, doko no kuni) = which country. State your country clearly.
responses.kanji: 分かりました。どこの国ですか？

phrases.kanji: 大使館に電話してください

phrases.japanese: いち、に、さん、よん、ご、ろく、なな、はち、きゅう、じゅう
phrases.romaji: Ichi, ni, san, shi, go, roku, nana, hachi, kyuu, juu
phrases.notes: 100 = ひゃく (百, hyaku), 1000 = せん (千, sen), 10000 = まん (万, man).

responses.japanese: 〜えんです
responses.listen_for: Numbers you need most: ひゃく (百, 100), せん (千, 1000), まん (万, 10,000). Most prices fall between 500–5000.
responses.kanji: 〜円です

phrases.kanji: 一、二、三、四、五、六、七、八、九、十

phrases.japanese: にんずうのかぞえかた
phrases.english: How to count people — the essential counters
phrases.notes: Japanese uses special words for counting people. 1 and 2 are irregular; from 3 onward, use number + にん (人, nin). Formal contexts (hotels, restaurants) use めい (名, mei) instead of にん (人). ひとり/いちめい (一人/一名, hitori/ichimei) = one, ふたり/にめい (二人/二名, futari/nimei) = two, さんにん/さんめい (三人/三名, san-nin/sanmei) = three — にん (人) is everyday, めい (名) is formal (hotel/restaurant).

responses.japanese: なんめいさまですか？
responses.english: How many people? (polite — what staff will ask)
responses.listen_for: なんめいさま (何名様, nanmei-sama) is the question that prompts you to answer with one of these counters. Hold up fingers as you answer.
responses.kanji: 何名様ですか？

responses.japanese: なんにんですか？
responses.listen_for: The everyday version of the same question, using にん (人) instead of the formal めい (名).
responses.kanji: 何人ですか？

phrases.japanese: なんじですか？
phrases.notes: じ (時, ji) = o'clock, ふん (分, fun) = minutes.

responses.japanese: 〜じ〜ふんです
responses.listen_for: Listen for the number before ほうr (時, hour) and before みぬてs (分, minutes). E.g., 3さんじはん (時半, sanji han) = 3:30.
responses.kanji: 〜時〜分です

phrases.japanese: 〜じによやくがあります
phrases.notes: Useful when arriving at a restaurant or hotel.

responses.japanese: おなまえをおねがいします
responses.listen_for: おなまえ (お名前, onamae) = name. Say your name clearly or show it written.
responses.kanji: お名前をお願いします

phrases.japanese: ひとり、ふたり、さんにん
phrases.english: One person, two people, three people
phrases.notes: The people-counter にん (人, nin) is irregular for 1 and 2: ひとり (一人, hitori), ふたり (二人, futari). From three onward it's regular: さんにん (三人, san-nin), よにん (四人, yo-nin), ごにん (五人, go-nin). Staff use the polite form 〜めいさま (名様, -mei-sama) instead, e.g. おひとりさま (お一人様, o-hitori-sama).

responses.japanese: なんめいさまですか？
responses.listen_for: Answer with ひとり/ふたり/さんにん (一人/二人/三人) etc., or just hold up fingers.
responses.kanji: 何名様ですか？

phrases.japanese: ひとつ、ふたつ、みっつ
phrases.notes: The generic item-counter つ (tsu) is used for food orders, souvenirs, and other countable objects when you don't know the specific counter: ひとつ, ふたつ, みっつ, よっつ, いつつ (一つ, 二つ, 三つ, 四つ, 五つ)... It stops being used after とお (十, too) = 10.

responses.japanese: いくつになさいますか？
responses.listen_for: いくつ (ikutsu) = how many — answer with ひとつ/ふたつ/みっつ (一つ/二つ/三つ).

phrases.japanese: 〜からきました
phrases.notes: Standard reply when asked where you are from.

responses.japanese: 〜からですか！とおいですね！
responses.romaji: [country] kara desu ka! Tooi desu ne!
responses.listen_for: とおい (遠い, tooi) = far. Japanese locals appreciate knowing where visitors are visiting from.
responses.kanji: 〜からですか！遠いですね！

phrases.japanese: にほんははじめてです
phrases.english: This is my first time in Japan
phrases.notes: If it's your second time, say: 2にかいめです (回目です, Nikaime desu).

responses.japanese: ようこそにほんへ！たのしんでくださいね
responses.romaji: Youkoso Nihon e! Tanoshinde kudasai ne
responses.english: Welcome to Japan! Please enjoy your stay
responses.listen_for: ようこそ (youkoso) = welcome. たのしんで (楽しんで, tanoshinde) = enjoy.
responses.kanji: ようこそ日本へ！楽しんでくださいね

phrases.japanese: にほんのごはんはとてもおいしいです
phrases.romaji: Nihon no gohan wa totemo oishii desu
phrases.notes: Guaranteed warm smile from locals.

responses.japanese: ほんとうですか？なにがいちばんすきですか？
responses.romaji: Hontou desu ka? Nani ga ichiban suki desu ka?
responses.english: Really? What do you like the most?
responses.listen_for: いちばんすき (一番好き, ichiban suki) = favorite/like the most. Name a dish like ラーメン or すし (寿司)!
responses.kanji: 本当ですか？何が一番好きですか？

phrases.kanji: 日本のご飯はとても美味しいです

phrases.japanese: きょうはさむいですね
phrases.notes: Great winter icebreaker in December.

responses.japanese: そうですね、かぜをひかないようにしてくださいね
responses.romaji: Sou desu ne, kaze wo hikanai you ni shite kudasai ne
responses.english: Indeed, make sure you stay warm and don't catch a cold
responses.listen_for: そうですね = 'I agree / indeed'. A universal casual agreement phrase.
responses.kanji: そうですね、風邪を引かないようにしてくださいね

phrases.japanese: しゃしんをとってもらえますか？
phrases.english: Could you take a photo for me?
phrases.notes: Hand over your phone or camera after asking.

responses.japanese: はい、いいですよ！はい、チーズ！
responses.romaji: Hai, ii desu yo! Hai, chiizu!
responses.listen_for: チーズ (chiizu) = cheese! Smile for the shutter.

phrases.kanji: 写真を撮ってもらえますか？

phrases.japanese: ここでしゃしんをとってもいいですか？
phrases.romaji: Koko de shashin wo totte mo ii desu ka?
phrases.english: May I take a photo here?
phrases.notes: Crucial at temples, shrines, or private collections.

responses.japanese: すみません、さつえいきんしです
responses.listen_for: さつえいきんし (撮影禁止, satsuei kinshi) = no photography allowed.
responses.kanji: すみません、撮影禁止です

phrases.kanji: ここで写真を撮ってもいいですか？

phrases.japanese: タトゥーはだいじょうぶですか？
phrases.notes: Check policies beforehand if you have visible ink.

responses.japanese: シールでかくせばだいじょうぶです
responses.english: It's fine if you cover them with a sticker
responses.listen_for: かくせば (隠せば, kakuseba) = if covered. They may offer cover-up patches.
responses.kanji: シールで隠せば大丈夫です

responses.japanese: もうしわけありませんが、おことわりしております
responses.romaji: Moushiwake arimasen ga, okotowari shite orimasu
responses.english: I'm sorry, but tattoos are not permitted
responses.listen_for: おことわり (お断り, okotowari) = refusal / not permitted.
responses.kanji: 申し訳ありませんが、お断りしております

phrases.kanji: タトゥーは大丈夫ですか？

phrases.japanese: ろてんぶろはどこですか？
phrases.notes: ろてんぶろ (露天風呂, rotenburo) = outdoor open-air bath.

responses.japanese: おくのかいだんをおりたところにございます
responses.romaji: Oku no kaidan wo orita tokoro ni gozaimasu
responses.english: It is located down the stairs at the back
responses.listen_for: おく (奥, oku) = back/inner part, かいだん (階段, kaidan) = stairs.
responses.kanji: 奥の階段を下りたところにございます

phrases.kanji: 露天風呂はどこですか？

phrases.japanese: タトゥーがあってもいれますか？
phrases.romaji: Tatoo ga atte mo hairemasu ka?
phrases.english: Can I enter even if I have a tattoo?
phrases.notes: More direct than a general check — useful when you already know you have visible ink. Many public onsen still ban tattoos due to their old association with the yakuza, though this is slowly changing, especially in tourist areas.

responses.japanese: ちいさいタトゥーならだいじょうぶです
responses.english: It's fine if the tattoo is small
responses.listen_for: ちいさい (小さい, chiisai) = small. Size-based policies are common.
responses.kanji: 小さいタトゥーなら大丈夫です

responses.japanese: もうしわけございませんが、タトゥーのあるほうはごえんりょいただいております
responses.romaji: Moushiwake gozaimasen ga, tatoo no aru kata wa goenryo itadaite orimasu
responses.english: I'm very sorry, but guests with tattoos are kindly asked not to enter
responses.listen_for: ごえんりょ (ご遠慮, goenryo) = a polite way of saying 'please refrain'. A firm but courteous no.
responses.kanji: 申し訳ございませんが、タトゥーのある方はご遠慮いただいております

phrases.kanji: タトゥーがあっても入れますか？

phrases.japanese: タトゥーをかくすシールはありますか？
phrases.romaji: Tatoo wo kakusu shiiru wa arimasu ka?
phrases.english: Do you have stickers to cover tattoos?
phrases.notes: Many tattoo-friendly onsen and sento sell or lend cover-up patches (シール/パッチ) at the front desk for guests with small tattoos.

responses.japanese: はい、フロントでおかいもとめいただけます
responses.english: Yes, you can purchase them at the front desk
responses.listen_for: フロント (furonto) = front desk. おかいもとめ (お買い求め, okaimotome) = a polite 'to purchase'.
responses.kanji: はい、フロントでお買い求めいただけます

responses.japanese: もうしわけありませんが、ごよういがございません
responses.romaji: Moushiwake arimasen ga, goyoui ga gozaimasen
responses.english: I'm sorry, we don't have any available
responses.listen_for: ごようい (ご用意, goyoui) = preparation/availability. A polite way to say 'we don't have that'.
responses.kanji: 申し訳ありませんが、ご用意がございません

phrases.kanji: タトゥーを隠すシールはありますか？

phrases.japanese: かしきりふろはありますか？
phrases.english: Do you have a private bath?
phrases.notes: かしきりぶろ (貸切風呂, kashikiri-buro) = a private/reservable bath, often booked by the hour — the easiest workaround if a facility doesn't allow visible tattoos in the shared baths.

responses.japanese: はい、ごよやくせいになっております
responses.english: Yes, it works on a reservation basis
responses.listen_for: ごよやくせい (ご予約制, goyoyaku-sei) = reservation system. Ask なんじから (何時から, nanji kara) for available times.
responses.kanji: はい、ご予約制になっております

responses.japanese: もうしわけございませんが、かしきりふろはございません
responses.romaji: Moushiwake gozaimasen ga, kashikiri-buro wa gozaimasen
responses.english: I'm sorry, we don't have a private bath
responses.listen_for: A polite no — you may need to look for a different facility.
responses.kanji: 申し訳ございませんが、貸切風呂はございません

phrases.kanji: 貸切風呂はありますか？

phrases.japanese: かしきりふろはなんにんまでいれますか？
phrases.romaji: Kashikiri-buro wa nan-nin made hairemasu ka?
phrases.english: How many people can use the private bath?
phrases.notes: Private baths (貸切風呂/家族風呂) are often capped at 2–4 people and booked in time slots — ask at check-in.

responses.japanese: ふたりまでです
responses.listen_for: まで (made) = up to/until — listen for the number right before it.
responses.kanji: 二人までです

responses.japanese: さいだいよんめいさままでごりよういただけます
responses.english: Up to a maximum of 4 people
responses.listen_for: めいさま (名様, mei-sama) is the polite counter for people, used by staff.
responses.kanji: 最大4名様までご利用いただけます

phrases.kanji: 貸切風呂は何人まで入れますか？

phrases.japanese: やっきょくはどこですか？
phrases.notes: やっきょく (薬局, yakkyoku) = pharmacy/drugstore. Look for ドラッグストア (doraggu sutoa) signs too — those also sell over-the-counter medicine.

responses.japanese: つぎのかくをみぎにまがったところにあります
responses.romaji: Tsugi no kado wo migi ni magatta tokoro ni arimasu
responses.english: It's just after you turn right at the next corner
responses.listen_for: つぎのかど (次の角, tsugi no kado) = next corner. みぎ/ひだり (右/左, migi/hidari) = right/left.
responses.kanji: 次の角を右に曲がったところにあります

phrases.japanese: ぐあいがわるいです
phrases.notes: A general catch-all for 'I don't feel well' — use it first, then get more specific if asked.

responses.japanese: だいじょうぶですか？どこがいたいですか？
responses.romaji: Daijoubu desu ka? Doko ga itai desu ka?
responses.english: Are you okay? Where does it hurt?
responses.listen_for: どこがどこがいたい (痛い, doko ga itai) = where does it hurt. Point to the area if you don't know the word.
responses.kanji: 大丈夫ですか？どこが痛いですか？

phrases.japanese: あたまがいたいです
phrases.notes: Swap あたま (頭, atama) / head for another body part + がいたいです (痛いです) to describe other pain, e.g. のど (喉, nodo) / throat, おなか (お腹, onaka) / stomach.

responses.japanese: ずつうやくをのみましたか？
responses.english: Have you taken any headache medicine?
responses.listen_for: のみました (飲みました, nomimashita) = took/drank. Medicine is 'drunk' (飲む) in Japanese, not 'taken'.
responses.kanji: 頭痛薬を飲みましたか？

phrases.japanese: おなかがいたいです
phrases.notes: Very common after trying unfamiliar food or drinking too much.

responses.japanese: たべすぎましたか？それとものみすぎましたか？
responses.english: Did you eat too much? Or drink too much?
responses.listen_for: すぎました (過ぎました, sugimashita) = did too much of something. たべ (食べ, tabe) = eat, のみ (飲み, nomi) = drink.
responses.kanji: 食べ過ぎましたか？それとも飲み過ぎましたか？

phrases.japanese: ねつがあります
phrases.notes: ねつ (熱, netsu) = fever/heat. Worth mentioning early since it signals something more serious than a minor ache.

responses.japanese: なんどくらいありますか？
responses.english: About how many degrees is it?
responses.listen_for: なんど (何度, nando) = how many degrees. Japan uses Celsius — 38さんじゅうはちど (度, sanjuu-hachi do) = 38°C.
responses.kanji: 何度くらいありますか？

phrases.japanese: かぜをひきました
phrases.notes: かぜ (風邪, kaze) = cold (illness) — note it's a different word from かぜ (風, kaze) / 'wind' despite similar spelling.

responses.japanese: おだいじに。ゆっくりやすんでくださいね
responses.romaji: Odaiji ni. Yukkuri yasunde kudasai ne
responses.english: Take care. Please get plenty of rest
responses.listen_for: おだいじに (お大事に, odaiji ni) = 'get well soon' — the standard thing to say to someone who's sick.
responses.kanji: お大事に。ゆっくり休んでくださいね

phrases.japanese: ずつうやくはありますか？
phrases.english: Do you have painkillers / headache medicine?
phrases.notes: ずつうやく (頭痛薬, zutsuuyaku) = headache medicine. For general pain relief ask for いたみどめ (痛み止め, itamidome) instead.

responses.japanese: はい、こちらのたなにございます
responses.romaji: Hai, kochira no tana ni gozaimasu
responses.listen_for: たな (棚, tana) = shelf. They'll likely point or walk you over.
responses.kanji: はい、こちらの棚にございます

phrases.japanese: ばんそうこうはありますか？
phrases.notes: ばんそうこう (絆創膏, bansoukou) = adhesive bandage/band-aid. Handy after a long day of walking in new shoes.

responses.japanese: はい、レジのちかくにあります
responses.romaji: Hai, reji no chikaku ni arimasu
responses.listen_for: レジ (reji) = cash register/checkout counter.
responses.kanji: はい、レジの近くにあります

phrases.japanese: 〇〇にアレルギーがあります
phrases.notes: Useful for both pharmacies and restaurants. Common fillers: ピーナッツ (peanuts), たまご (卵, tamago) / eggs, こむぎ (小麦, komugi) / wheat, こうかくるい (甲殻類, koukakurui) / shellfish.

responses.japanese: わかりました、かくにんいたします
responses.listen_for: かくにん (確認, kakunin) = confirm/check. They're taking your allergy seriously.
responses.kanji: 分かりました、確認いたします

phrases.japanese: びょういんにいきたいです
phrases.english: I want to go to a hospital/clinic
phrases.notes: びょういん (病院, byouin) covers both hospitals and small clinics in everyday use. For something urgent, see the Emergencies scenario instead.

responses.japanese: ちかくにびょういんがあります。ごあんないしましょうか？
responses.romaji: Chikaku ni byouin ga arimasu. Goannai shimashou ka?
responses.english: There's a hospital nearby. Shall I show you the way?
responses.listen_for: ごあんない (ご案内, goannai) = guide/show the way. A kind offer — say はい、おねがいします (お願いします) if you want help.
responses.kanji: 近くに病院があります。ご案内しましょうか？

phrases.japanese: はじめまして、わたしのなまえは〇〇です
phrases.romaji: Hajimemashite, watashi no namae wa [name] desu
phrases.english: Nice to meet you, my name is ___
phrases.notes: Swap 〇〇 for your name. Standard way to open a self-introduction.

responses.japanese: はじめまして、〇〇です。よろしくおねがいします
responses.english: Nice to meet you too, I'm ___. Pleased to meet you
responses.listen_for: They'll introduce themselves back — remember their name if you can.
responses.kanji: はじめまして、〇〇です。よろしくお願いします

phrases.kanji: はじめまして、私の名前は〇〇です

phrases.japanese: わたしは〇〇じんです
phrases.notes: Add じん (人, jin) after your country's adjective form, e.g. アメリカあめりかん (人, American), イギリスbりちsh (人, British), フランスfれんch (人, French), カナダかなぢあん (人, Canadian).

responses.japanese: そうですか、〇〇からきたんですね！
responses.romaji: Sou desu ka, [country] kara kitan desu ne!
responses.english: Oh I see, so you came from ___!
responses.listen_for: からからきた (来た, kara kita) = came from. They're confirming your home country.
responses.kanji: そうですか、〇〇から来たんですね！

phrases.japanese: しごとは〇〇です
phrases.notes: Common jobs: エンジニア (engineer), デザイナー (designer), てあちぇr (先生, teacher), おっふぃけをrけr (会社員, office worker), sつでんt (学生, student).

responses.japanese: 〇〇のおしごとですか、すごいですね！
responses.romaji: [job] no oshigoto desu ka, sugoi desu ne!
responses.english: Oh, you work as ___? That's great!
responses.listen_for: すごい (sugoi) = amazing/impressive. A common polite compliment.
responses.kanji: 〇〇のお仕事ですか、すごいですね！

phrases.japanese: 〇〇ではたらいています
phrases.notes: Use for a company name or industry, e.g. ITいtこmぱんy (企業, IT company), ほsぴたl (病院, hospital).

responses.japanese: へえ、おもしろいおしごとですね
responses.english: Oh wow, that sounds like an interesting job
responses.listen_for: へえ (hee) = a casual 'oh wow' / interested reaction.
responses.kanji: へえ、面白いお仕事ですね

phrases.japanese: けっこんしています
phrases.notes: If single, say どくしんです (独身です, Dokushin desu) instead.

responses.japanese: そうなんですね！おこさんはいますか？
responses.romaji: Sou nan desu ne! Okosan wa imasu ka?
responses.english: I see! Do you have kids?
responses.listen_for: おこさん (お子さん, okosan) = a polite way to say 'your child(ren)'.
responses.kanji: そうなんですね！お子さんはいますか？

phrases.japanese: こどもが〇にんいます
phrases.notes: No kids? Say こどもわいません (子供はいません, Kodomo wa imasen). ひとり (一人, hitori)=1, ふたり (二人, futari)=2, さんにん (三人, san-nin)=3.

responses.japanese: かわいいでしょうね！
responses.listen_for: A warm, common reaction — no response needed beyond a smile and ありがとうございます.

phrases.japanese: にほんの〇〇がだいすきです
phrases.notes: Great compliment and conversation starter. Fill in たべもの (食べ物, tabemono) / food, ぶんか (文化, bunka) / culture, しぜん (自然, shizen) / nature, ひと (人, hito) / people.

responses.japanese: ありがとうございます！にほんにきてよかったですね
responses.romaji: Arigatou gozaimasu! Nihon ni kite yokatta desu ne
responses.english: Thank you! I'm glad you came to Japan
responses.listen_for: きてよかった (来てよかった, kite yokatta) = glad you came. A warm, proud response.
responses.kanji: ありがとうございます！日本に来てよかったですね

phrases.japanese: あなたは？
phrases.notes: The easiest way to turn any statement about yourself back into a question — keeps the conversation natural.

responses.japanese: わたしもおなじです！
responses.listen_for: おなじ (同じ, onaji) = same. A friendly sign you have something in common.
responses.kanji: 私も同じです！
